prompt: Create an ORIGINAL production sprite atlas for a cozy mobile game called Mochi Arcade, Jelly Slice. TRANSPARENT background. Twelve isolated sprites arranged as EXACTLY 4 rows by 3 columns, generous empty gutters, each object fully visible, no text, no labels, no grid, no ground, no drop shadow. Portrait sheet with a 3:4 ratio. Each ROW is a different plump jelly fruit: row 1 strawberry pink rounded heart with tiny green leaf; row 2 mandarin orange round with little green leaf; row 3 kiwi green round with brown thin rind; row 4 purple grape round jelly with small leaf. Each row's COLUMN 1 is the complete whole fruit, softly rounded, tiny cocoa eyes and smile; COLUMN 2 is that exact same fruit's LEFT HALF sliced vertically; COLUMN 3 is its complementary RIGHT HALF sliced vertically. Every half shows a beautiful clean translucent jelly cut face, appropriate seeds/segments, matching rind and color of its whole. A pair of halves together should visibly read as the whole cut into two. Each half has roughly half the width of the whole, but the same height and visual scale; center each piece in its cell. The halves have no duplicated full face. All sprites are front view with slight depth and glossy jelly highlights, pale watercolor-gouache texture, warm cocoa fine edges, soft pastel strawberry pink, apricot, pistachio and lilac; cohesive cream stationery game art. Smooth clean alpha silhouettes, high readability at 80 pixel diameter, no photorealism, no 3D scene, no tray, no typography, no watermark. Maintain uniform scales across all rows. Each complete fruit about 75% of cell height, generous gutters separating every sprite.
